listing_view.reasoning: There is no subscription, grey market, anchor, or demand data of any kind, and the issue has not opened, so a listing view is not possible from what I was given. The apparent discount (51.6x vs a stated benchmark of 128.1x) means nothing until the benchmark's composition is verifiable.

longterm_view.reasoning: Operating cash flow was negative in two of the last three years (-117.64m and -266.44m before turning positive at 97.85m) and free cash flow was deeply negative in two of three years, meaning earnings are not converting to cash. Customer relationships averaging over nine years [business, page 219] and vertical integration [business, page 221] are genuine positives, but no ROE, ROCE, or balance sheet figures were available to judge capital efficiency.

governance.reasoning: No criminal proceedings against promoters and no SEBI penalties are disclosed [litigation, page 408 and page 409], but promoter funds are pledged as margin money against borrowings [promoters, page 332] and an ESOP granted at Rs 212.96 [promoters, page 357] sits suspiciously close to the IPO band of 258-272.

key_risks.risk: Negative operating and free cash flow
key_risks.why_it_matters: Cash conversion failed in two of three years, so the P/E multiple is priced on accounting profits the business has not yet collected.
The 128x benchmark average that makes this look 'cheap' at 51.6x could not be checked against any parsed peer row, so the discount may be manufactured by peer selection.
Promoter funds of Rs 73.51-77.32 million are locked as margin against borrowings and guarantees, signalling a leveraged promoter balance sheet that can force selling under stress.
4,96,024 options granted in June 2025 at Rs 212.96, just below the IPO price floor, transfer upside to insiders immediately before the public pays the listing multiple.

answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: I cannot verify this. The document claims a peer/benchmark average P/E of 128.11, against which this issue at ~51.6x looks cheap, but zero peer rows could be parsed from what was given, so I cannot confirm who the peers are or whether they are themselves wildly overpriced. A 128x average for cable makers would itself suggest the peers are expensive rather than this being cheap; treat the 'discount' as seller's framing, not evidence.
answers.citation: not answerable from what I was given

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A verifiable peer table with named companies and P/Es, plus audited balance sheet and ROE/ROCE figures, would let me judge both the valuation claim and capital quality. Evidence that the latest year's positive operating cash flow is structural (receivable days falling) rather than a one-off would lift the long-term score materially.
